Quote: Eeyore, 2005-05-19T01:52:38Z
As for how you did it. I suspect you opened it up in notepad or wordpard and click save. Even if you dont change anything saving corrupts the .sol. This is because in the .sol there are charachters that notepad/wordpad dont understand. So they convert it to something that they do understand so as to display it to you. By clicking save you are then overwriting the charachters that notepad/wordpad doesnt understand with the charchters that they replaces them with.
i don't think it's that the notepad doesn't understand the characters, but doesn't know how to display it. the characters will contain the information it needs, i believe, but if editted, will be corrupted. although, this could not be the issue because i only opened it with word after it had already erased my 90's column. although, the first part seems to sound correct, in some way.

i didn't really get that, but i'll try...

Edit: okay, here's what i've discovered. and if i read nevermore's post, i would've discovered this...

2^768,564,-1,0 = a launch pad

2^ represents launch pad.
768 determines the x axis [the higher the more right it is]
564 determines the y axis [the higher the lower]
-1 determines the horizontal strength [lower the stronger]
0 determines vertical strength

if the launch pad is facing left, then the lower the -1 is, the stronger. however if it's facing right, the more positive the stronger. i still don't understand how to make you teleport however. he just boosts off the map.

usually, i just try to come up with a cool tileset, first usually using the [1] tiles. i just mess around with it, trying to get something that looks good. at the same time, i plan ways how the tileset can work together, so i edit tiles, move them around, copy them, etc. usually, i work with symmetrical tilesets. or at least i start with them. #79859 3 2005-06-30T06:31:58Z Eldrial
NaN doesn't turn up in Search, so i'll briefly explain it here:

Say you make a level. You finished, and you copied the data into a notepad to save it, blah blah blah. Later, you return to it to play it. You paste the level data into the Level Data box [the top box in the debug menu], and you press [L] to load the level. But when you pressed [L], you didn't click out of the Level Data box. Therefore, your 'typing cursor' is still in the box. So, when you pressed [L], you typed that letter into the data box, adding a letter to the data. Because letters don't exist in level datas, it was invalid. So you added a letter and loaded the level at the same time, but since the letter was added.... yeah. It didn't make sense to the game.

Overall, that just makes the level a little messed up, causing objects misplaced. Misplaced onto the border. I'm not quite sure how this is fixable... So you have to be careful.

Appearance

Simple jumping factors, only the trail and places to go were at some points vaugue for the beginner players - thus the area displayed advanced jumping techniques. 6 points

maximo Float Park

Beautifully placed bounce blocks. The only flaw was the launch pads that appeared to be placed in the middle of no where, even if served great purpose. 4 points

Loading time/lag
Surprisingly little loading time/lag considering 95% of it was objects. 4 points

Ease of use
Bounce blocks are an extremely tricky object as N players need the most training in them, making the techniques in this map difficult than others. Still, simple techniques clearly available. 5 points

Fun factor
Extremely fun. Especially when close calls or such advanced tricks are pulled off. An exceedingly amusing level. More challenge with the released homing launcher made it even better. 19 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
Countless things. Countless tricks can be pulled off. An excellent training with the most needed training of all time. Homing launchers on bounce blocks. An amazing map. 28 points

Ninja rating
4 points

Originality
Though slightly common, it still contained traits that were unique like some placement of bounce blocks, and the trap door trick to have the homing launcher open at all times. 8 points

Overall thoughts on map
I absolutely loved it. It is the greatest training in the most needed area. I loved the possible removal of accidental shutting out the homing launcher. So many great possibilities lie within the map. Could move at a slow pace, or with the right techniques extreme speed. Spectacular play park. 10 points

TOTAL 82 points

i know, nevermore. it's not meant to be an excuse, just saying why, at least i, haven't been judging very much. i'm not saying that i don't want to be judging these maps, or that i'm not taking this to be my responsibility. though, here it is.

rrrobyp R3park[/color]

Appearance
A simple appearance; large loops, several bounce blocks and a couple thwumps. 4 points

Loading time/lag
5 points

Ease of use
A challenge for long jumps with the loops. Nothing too difficult to do. Although, the two thwumps on the right were difficult to use. 8 points

Fun factor
The map felt limitted as the things to do on the map only had one purpose. No multipurposes. Thus, the map involved a lot of repeating itself. But what there was to do proved to be pretty enjoyable. 14 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
I particularly found the thwump areas pretty innovatative and smooth. A good practice with loops. 20 points

Ninja rating
2 points

Originality
Nothing too unique except for the two thwumps on the right which I found pretty interesting. 7 points

Overall thoughts on map
A pretty fun map, good for loops as said before. The thwumps were a good addition. 6 points

TOTAL 66 points

________________________

The Daily Llama Steamy Pile of PC[/color]

Appearance
It appears to be a large jumble tiles. Not a pretty appearance. Still, its intriguing with the launch pads and one-ways. 3 points

Loading time/lag
Very little load time. 5 points

Ease of use
Very difficult level, as routes are hazy and the launch pads can get confusing especially the left and right ones. Takes several runs around to get used to it. 2 points

Fun factor
As difficult as it is to use, fun can be found once you are adjusted to the style of the level. Still, finding the flow to this level gets tedious and annoying. 10 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
Advanced tehcniques are very well possible, but difficult to see. The level had a good idea with the launch pads, but very difficult to use these pads as intended. 16 points

Ninja rating
2 points

Originality
Different from what has been done before. 12 points

Overall thoughts on map
I thought that The Daily Llama was on the correct track, but should aim for something slightly easier to use. 6 points

TOTAL 56 points

________________________

great_sea Djembe[/color]

Appearance
A very simple appearance with the scattered tile shards and simple loops. Making the large tiles seem like an outline was only pleasing to the eye. 4 points

Loading time/lag
Only two objects. N and a launch pad. 5 points

Ease of use
Very simple map. Basic [wall] jumping on small tiles, a couple loops, etc. A lot of possible advanced techniques and beginners also. 9 points

Fun factor
A lot of exhilerating jumps are very possible and quite clear to execute. Quite fun doing chain jumps on the small tiles. 17 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
I only found one main thing N can do on the map in general: plain jumping. Though, there are a lot of jumping possibilities (eg, chain jumping, wall jumping off small tiles). I found the small tiles excellent as it can practice precision jumping. Also, the several sides on these small tiles made it multipurpose as you can jump on it from different sides. 21 points

Ninja rating
3 points

Originality
Though a good map, nothing unique. 2 points

Overall thoughts on map
An excellent practice for basic jumping. Not much of anything else, however. Still, a very good beginner map. 8 points

TOTAL 69 points

________________________

Andrelius Break a Leg[/color]

Appearance
The loops were overdone, and the launch pads isnt very appealing being in midair. 2 points

Loading time/lag
5 points

Ease of use
As loops are usually incredibly easy to use, this level oddly makes it difficult as they are too large and uneven tiles. 4 points

Fun factor
Gets very dull after one round around the level. 5 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
Not many great things N can do at all except have an attempt at making it around the large loops. The launch pads did not even work very well, as one of them will shoot you against the tile and kill you. The bounce blocks also proved to be unuseful. 6 points

Ninja rating
0 points

Originality
Nothing really unique. Just plain loops. 1 point

Overall thoughts on map
I really had low thoughts for this map. It only contained uneven loops, the objects didnt fulfill its purpose. Mainly the right launch pad which would often launch you into the tile which would result in death rather than a speed boost. The things to do on the map were exceedingly limitted and dull. 1 point

TOTAL 24 points

________________________

snuggletummy Dare Devil Park[/color]

Appearance
Pretty horrible. Mainly the bottom area. The countless unrendered [1] tiles inside the slope ruined the appearance, and the [4] tiles in the center also makes it worse as it doesnt match the [1] tiles. 0 points

Loading time/lag
Quite a few objects made a slightly longer load time, and the several laser drones also made the game lag a little. 3 points

Ease of use
A strange level, but pretty easy to use. Using the launch pads to rise to the top level, and dodging the two rockets on bounce blocks. 7 points

Fun factor
Very dull. The laser drones will only shoot at the center area of the top level, and typicly does nothing as N only jumps across the center area to reach the other side. The rockets are pretty easy to dodge, and it easily gets repetetive. 4 points

Quality & Quantity of cool stuff N can do on the map
Very little to do on this level, as its just dodging a couple rockets and waiting for the laser drones in the center to stop to cross of the other side, only to continue dodging the two rockets. 6 points

Ninja rating
1 point

Originality
The laser drones were different, even if it didnt do anything good. 5 points

Overall thoughts on the map
Very dull and repetetive. 2 points

#5508 1 2005-12-03T00:28:36Z Eldrial
For those wondering, "How can I get my N save file to another computer?" or "How can I restart N?", here's what you'll need to know.

*Note: I do not have the magical power to recreate .sol files. If you have lost yours, do not contact me about getting your progress back. It's gone. What you can do is read this guide to learn how to prevent future occurrences.

Introduction

The n_v14b_userdata.sol, or ".sol", is the file that contains all your N peference datas. That includes your Configuration settings, your progress in your game, your personal bests, etc. With this file, you can move around your progress in the game to other computers and such so that you won't need to start all over on a new computer, as that can be quite tiresome.

Its Location

Windows 2000, XP:
C:\Documents and Settings\Username\Application Data\Macromedia\Flash Player\#SharedObjects\random series of letters and numbers\localhost

Windows 95, Me:
C:\Windows\Application Data\Macromedia\Flash Player\#SharedObjects\random series of letters and numbers\localhost

*Application Data and subfolders will be hidden.[/i]

To be able to see the files:
  • Go to Control Panel > Folder Options > View.Select the option to show hidden files or folders.
  • A simple way to find your .sol file is to use the Search program. Search for All Files and Folders. Type in .sol in the first box. Before engaging the search, drop down to More Advanced Options and be sure that "Search system folders", "Search hidden files and folders", and "Search subfolders" are checked.
Mac OS 9:
Macintosh HD/System Folder/Preferences/Macromedia/Flash Player/#Shared Objects/random string of letters and numbers/localhost

Mac OS X;
/Users/Short name/Library/Preferences/Macromedia/Flash Player/#SharedObjects/random series of letters and numbers/localhost

Using the Files

.sol must always be located in these locations. When moving the file from computer to computer, be sure to place it in the correct folder, or else N will not read the .sol you're trying to use. Do not have more than one of the same type of .sol in the folder.

*You should always keep a backup .sol file. It's not the best thing to happen to lose all your progress that you've worked long and hard for. So if you're moving around .sol files, keep a backup somewhere in case it gets lost or corrupted. Keep the backup in a seperate folder.

Never open a .sol file, unless you have a backup and you know what you're doing. If you decide to try to pry through the file, make sure you have a backup as messing around with .sol files can easily corrupt them.

When copying .sol files into an e-mail to move it to a different computer or for similar reasons, be sure to Zip or compress the files, as most e-mail domains will take the file as a text file and not function correctly when saved.

Concerning .sol files

**Never ask for a .sol file, as you will never legitimately receive one from any member of the forum. Never publicly distribute .sol files to beggars. Your post will deleted and warned depending on the cicumstances.

* * * * * *

If you have any further questions, PM me or ask away here!
